_info: Registro: call center → oficina. Cada par tiene la frase de call center, la versión corporativa natural, dos distractores (uno todavía demasiado guionado y otro demasiado brusco) y una nota. 'category' debe coincidir con el id de una categoría.

categories.title: Disculpas
categories.rule: Entre colegas, la disculpa es corta y va seguida de la solución.
categories.explanation: «I do apologize for the inconvenience» suena a guion. En la oficina: Sorry about that / My mistake — here's the fix. Guardá «I apologize» para errores serios con clientes.

categories.title: Avisos
categories.rule: Los avisos van directo al punto: Heads-up, Quick update, FYI.
categories.explanation: «Please be advised», «Kindly note», «This is to inform you» suenan a carta legal o a plantilla. Un aviso de oficina dice qué cambió y, si hace falta, qué hacer.

categories.title: Pedidos
categories.rule: Para pedir algo: Could you…? · Let me know… · Does [hora] work for you?
categories.explanation: «Kindly», «revert back», «at your earliest convenience», «do the needful» son típicos del inglés de call center o de India y suenan rígidos en EE. UU. Pedir de forma simple no es descortés.

categories.title: Seguimiento
categories.rule: Para retomar un tema: Following up on… · Any update on…? · Just to recap…
categories.explanation: «As per our previous conversation» es burocrático y «Per my last email» suena pasivo-agresivo. Un seguimiento natural es breve y amable.

categories.title: Respuestas
categories.rule: Responder con iniciativa: Sure, I'll take care of it · Got it · Thanks for flagging this.
categories.explanation: Las respuestas de guion («It is my pleasure to assist you», «I will escalate this to the appropriate department») suenan aprendidas. En la oficina se responde corto y con la acción concreta.

categories.title: Saludos y cierres
categories.rule: Saludos y cierres cortos: Hi team · Hope your week's going well · Let me know if you have any questions.
categories.explanation: En emails internos no hace falta «Dear Sir or Madam» ni «Please do not hesitate to contact me». Lo natural es breve y cálido.

categories.title: Esperas y transferencias
categories.rule: Para pedir un momento o pasar a alguien: One sec · Let me connect you with [persona].
categories.explanation: «May I place you on a brief hold?» y «I will proceed to transfer your call to the corresponding department» son puro call center. En una oficina se nombra a la persona y se habla simple.

pairs.callcenter: I do apologize for the inconvenience.
pairs.corporate: Sorry about that!
distractors: Please accept my sincere apologies for any inconvenience caused.
My bad, whatever.
pairs.note: Entre colegas, una disculpa corta suena segura. «I do apologize» con «do» enfático es marca registrada del call center.

pairs.callcenter: I apologize for the delay in my response.
pairs.corporate: Sorry for the slow reply!
distractors: Please excuse the delay in our response time.
Sorry, I didn't feel like answering.
pairs.note: En emails internos, «Sorry for the slow reply» o «Sorry for the delay» es lo normal.

pairs.callcenter: We regret to inform you that the shipment has been delayed.
pairs.corporate: Quick update: the shipment's running late.
distractors: Please be informed that the shipment has suffered a delay.
Bad news, the shipment's dead.
pairs.note: «We regret to inform you» es de carta formal. En la oficina se da la noticia directo, con «Quick update».

pairs.context: Colega molesto por un error del sistema
pairs.callcenter: I understand your frustration.
pairs.corporate: That's frustrating — let's get it sorted.
distractors: I completely understand your frustration and I am here to assist you.
Calm down, it's not a big deal.
pairs.note: La frase empática de guion suena aprendida. Reconocé el problema y pasá a la acción: «let's get it sorted».

pairs.callcenter: Sorry for any confusion this may have caused.
pairs.corporate: Sorry, my mistake — here's the right version.
distractors: We apologize for any confusion this may have caused.
Sorry if you got confused.
pairs.note: Asumir el error en primera persona («my mistake») y dar la solución suena profesional.

pairs.callcenter: Please be advised that the meeting was moved.
pairs.corporate: Heads-up, the meeting moved to 3.
distractors: Kindly be informed that the meeting has been rescheduled.
FYI meeting moved, deal with it.
pairs.note: «Please be advised» suena a aviso legal. «Heads-up» es el aviso amistoso típico de oficina.

pairs.callcenter: Kindly note that the office will be closed on Friday.
pairs.corporate: Just a reminder: the office is closed Friday.
distractors: Please be advised that the office will remain closed on Friday.
Office closed Friday, don't come.
pairs.note: «Kindly» es muy típico del inglés de call center; en EE. UU. suena anticuado.

pairs.callcenter: This is to inform you that your request has been processed.
pairs.corporate: All done — your request went through.
distractors: Please be informed that your request has been successfully processed.
Done. Next.
pairs.note: «This is to inform you» es de plantilla. En persona o en Slack, ve al grano.

pairs.callcenter: Please be informed that the system will be down for maintenance.
pairs.corporate: FYI, the system will be down for maintenance tonight.
distractors: Kindly be advised of the scheduled system maintenance.
System's broken tonight lol.
pairs.note: «FYI» es perfectamente aceptable en emails internos y Slack.

pairs.callcenter: As per our records, the invoice is still pending.
pairs.corporate: Looks like the invoice is still pending.
distractors: According to our records, the aforementioned invoice remains pending.
You didn't pay the invoice.
pairs.note: «As per our records» suena a cobranza. «Looks like…» suaviza y suena colaborativo.

pairs.callcenter: Kindly confirm your availability.
pairs.corporate: Does Thursday at 10 work for you?
distractors: Please confirm your availability at your earliest convenience.
Tell me when you're free.
pairs.note: Proponer una hora concreta ahorra idas y vueltas: es lo que hace una buena asistente ejecutiva.

pairs.callcenter: Please revert back to me at your earliest convenience.
pairs.corporate: Let me know when you get a chance.
distractors: Kindly revert at the earliest.
Answer me ASAP.
pairs.note: «Revert» como «responder» no se usa en EE. UU., y «at your earliest convenience» es muy rígido.

pairs.callcenter: Revert back to me.
pairs.corporate: Get back to me.
distractors: Kindly revert to me.
Reply me back.
pairs.note: «Revert» significa volver a un estado anterior. Para «respondeme»: get back to me.

pairs.callcenter: May I kindly request the purchase order number?
pairs.corporate: Could you send me the PO number?
distractors: I would like to kindly request that you provide the PO number.
Give me the PO number.
pairs.note: «Could you…?» es la forma estándar y cortés de pedir algo entre colegas.

pairs.callcenter: I would like to request your assistance with this matter.
pairs.corporate: Could you help me with this?
distractors: I hereby request your kind assistance regarding this matter.
Help me with this.
pairs.note: Pedir ayuda de forma simple y directa no es descortés; lo largo suena distante.

pairs.callcenter: Please do the needful.
pairs.corporate: Could you take care of this?
distractors: Kindly do the necessary at the earliest.
Do it.
pairs.note: «Do the needful» es inglés de India; en EE. UU. suena raro o directamente no se entiende.

pairs.callcenter: Please find attached the requested document.
pairs.corporate: Here's the file you asked for.
distractors: Attached herewith please find the requested document.
File attached. Check it.
pairs.note: «Please find attached» no es un error, pero «Here's…» o «I've attached…» suena más moderno y cálido.

pairs.callcenter: Please review it at your earliest convenience.
pairs.corporate: Could you take a look when you have a minute?
distractors: Kindly review the same at the earliest possible opportunity.
Review it now.
pairs.note: «Take a look» y «when you have a minute» son la manera natural de pedir sin presionar.

pairs.context: Email a un colega de otra área
pairs.callcenter: Would you be so kind as to send me the report?
pairs.corporate: Could you send me the report when you get a chance?
distractors: I would be most grateful if you could kindly send the report.
Send me the report.
pairs.note: «Would you be so kind as to…» suena teatral. «When you get a chance» es cortés sin exagerar.

pairs.callcenter: As per our previous conversation…
pairs.corporate: Following up on our chat…
distractors: As per our earlier telephonic conversation…
Like I told you before…
pairs.note: «As per» suena burocrático; «Following up on…» es la apertura clásica de seguimiento.

pairs.callcenter: I am writing to follow up regarding my previous email.
pairs.corporate: Just following up on my last email.
distractors: This is a follow-up regarding the previous email sent by me.
Why didn't you answer my email?
pairs.note: «Just following up» es breve y amable; no reprocha que no te hayan contestado.

pairs.callcenter: I am calling to inquire about the status of the order.
pairs.corporate: Any update on the order?
distractors: I would like to inquire regarding the current status of the order.
Where's my order?
pairs.note: «Inquire» es formal; «Any update on…?» es la pregunta corta típica en Slack o email.

pairs.context: Terminando una charla con tu jefe
pairs.callcenter: Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
pairs.corporate: Anything else you need from me?
distractors: Is there anything further I may help you with at this time?
Are we done?
pairs.note: La pregunta de cierre del call center delata el guion. Con tu jefe, más corta.

pairs.context: Después de hacer esperar a alguien
pairs.callcenter: Thank you for your patience.
pairs.corporate: Thanks for bearing with me.
distractors: We appreciate your patience and understanding.
Finally, right?
pairs.note: «Thanks for bearing with me» reconoce la espera en primera persona y suena humano.

pairs.callcenter: Per my last email…
pairs.corporate: Just to recap…
distractors: As stated in my previous email…
Like I already said…
pairs.note: «Per my last email» suena pasivo-agresivo en EE. UU. «Just to recap» resume sin reprochar.

pairs.callcenter: Understood.
pairs.corporate: Got it, thanks.
distractors: Your request has been duly noted.
Roger that.
pairs.note: «Understood» suena militar. «Got it» es el «entendido» natural.

pairs.callcenter: Noted with thanks.
pairs.corporate: Thanks, got it!
distractors: Duly noted, thank you.
K.
pairs.note: «Noted with thanks» y «duly noted» son de plantilla; «Thanks, got it!» suena cercano.

pairs.callcenter: It is my pleasure to assist you.
pairs.corporate: Happy to help!
distractors: It was my pleasure assisting you today.
Yeah, whatever.
pairs.note: «Happy to help» es la respuesta estándar entre colegas.

pairs.callcenter: Certainly, I can help you with that.
pairs.corporate: Sure, I'll take care of it.
distractors: Absolutely, I will be more than happy to assist you with that.
Fine, I'll do it.
pairs.note: «More than happy to assist» es guion clásico; «I'll take care of it» muestra iniciativa y ownership.

pairs.context: Algo que no te toca resolver
pairs.callcenter: I will escalate this to the appropriate department.
pairs.corporate: I'll loop in the right person.
distractors: I will be forwarding your concern to the corresponding area.
That's not my job.
pairs.note: «Loop in» = incluir a alguien en la conversación. Muy usado en consultoras.

pairs.callcenter: Allow me to check that information for you.
pairs.corporate: Let me check and get back to you.
distractors: Please allow me a moment to verify that information.
Wait.
pairs.note: «Let me check and get back to you» es la frase de oro cuando no sabés algo en el momento.

pairs.callcenter: I completely understand your concern.
pairs.corporate: Good point — let me look into it.
distractors: I truly understand your concern and I apologize for any inconvenience.
Not my problem.
pairs.note: Validar («Good point») y actuar («let me look into it») vale más que la empatía de guion.

pairs.context: Un colega te avisa de un error
pairs.callcenter: Thank you for bringing this to my attention.
pairs.corporate: Thanks for flagging this.
distractors: I appreciate you bringing this matter to my attention.
OK, I see.
pairs.note: «Flag» = señalar un problema. Muy común en entornos corporativos.

pairs.context: Contestando el teléfono de tu jefe
pairs.callcenter: Thank you for calling, my name is Fio, how may I help you?
pairs.corporate: Good morning, Mr. Lee's office, this is Fio.
distractors: Thank you for contacting the executive office, how may I assist you today?
Yeah? Who's this?
pairs.note: Una asistente ejecutiva se identifica con la oficina y su nombre, sin el guion completo.

pairs.callcenter: Have a wonderful rest of your day!
pairs.corporate: Have a good one!
distractors: I wish you a very pleasant remainder of your day.
Bye then.
pairs.note: «Have a good one» es la despedida casual más común en EE. UU.

pairs.callcenter: I hope this email finds you well.
pairs.corporate: Hi Sarah, hope your week's going well!
distractors: I hope this email finds you in good health and spirits.
Hey you.
pairs.note: No es un error, pero está tan gastada que suena automática. Personalizala con el nombre.

pairs.callcenter: Dear Sir or Madam,
pairs.corporate: Hi team,
distractors: To whom it may concern,
Yo guys,
pairs.note: «Dear Sir or Madam» es para cartas a desconocidos. Internamente: «Hi team» o «Hi all».

pairs.callcenter: Please do not hesitate to contact me should you have any questions.
pairs.corporate: Let me know if you have any questions.
distractors: Should you require any further assistance, please do not hesitate to reach out.
Ask me if you don't get it.
pairs.note: El cierre corto es el estándar en emails internos.

pairs.callcenter: It was a pleasure speaking with you today.
pairs.corporate: Thanks for the quick chat!
distractors: It has been a pleasure to speak with you on this call.
OK bye.
pairs.note: Entre colegas, agradecé la charla en concreto: «Thanks for the quick chat».

pairs.callcenter: May I place you on a brief hold?
pairs.corporate: Can you give me a sec?
distractors: Would you mind if I placed you on a brief hold?
Wait there.
pairs.note: «Give me a sec» o «One sec» es lo natural fuera de un call center.

pairs.callcenter: Thank you for holding.
pairs.corporate: Thanks for waiting — I'm back.
distractors: Thank you for your patience while on hold.
Back. What did you want?
pairs.note: Simple y humano: «Thanks for waiting».

pairs.callcenter: I will transfer your call to the corresponding department.
pairs.corporate: Let me connect you with Ana in Finance.
distractors: I am going to proceed to transfer your call to the corresponding area.
Not my area, call someone else.
pairs.note: «Corresponding» es calco de «correspondiente». Nombrá a la persona o al área.

pairs.callcenter: Please bear with me while I pull up your information.
pairs.corporate: One sec, I'm pulling it up.
distractors: Kindly bear with me while I access your file.
Wait, the system is slow.
pairs.note: «Pull up» = abrir/buscar información en pantalla. Muy natural.

pairs.callcenter: I'm going to proceed to send you the email.
pairs.corporate: I'll send you the email now.
distractors: I will proceed with the sending of the email.
Email's coming, chill.
pairs.note: «Proceed to» es calco de «procedo a». En inglés: I'll + verbo.
